newsitem.title: USA: Weak U.S. Sept housing starts mask sector strength.
newsitem.headline: Weak U.S. Sept housing starts mask sector strength.

text.p: A surprisingly low level of new housing starts in September runs counter to the strength in recent mortgage applications data, suggesting starts levels may rebound in the months ahead, economists said on Thursday.
"I have difficulty buying into the story that housing is weak given that mortgage applications remain strong," said Mary Dennis, a senior economist at Merrill Lynch and Co Inc.
"I think this is more of a little correction or a pause rather than a new trend," she added.

The Commerce Department reported on Thursday that housing starts fell by a sizable 6.0 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.438 million versus a revised rate of 1.529 million in the previous month.
The decline represented the largest drop since January of 1995 when starts fell at a 9.0 percent rate. Wall Street economists had forecast September starts at a 1.47 million unit annual rate.
The numbers appeared to confirm the trend seen Wednesday in the National Association of Home Builders' Housing Market Index, which fell to 53 in October from 56 in September.
But they stood in direct contrast to mortgage applications data released by the Mortgage Bankers Association of America (MBA) on Thursday morning.

The MBA reported that the volume of U.S. mortgage applications rose 7.3 percent in the week ended October 11. The volume of applications to refinance mortgages jumped 19.3 percent in the survey week while applications to purchase mortgages rose 4.1 percent.
In the MBA report the seasonally adjusted refinancing index rose 19.3 percent to 324.8 from 272.3 in the previous week while the purchase index climbed 3.7 percent to 189.1.
"The mortgage applications index suggests that we'll stay in this range (on starts) near the high side for a while," said Lee Youngdahl, money market economist at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co Inc.
"The purchase index was up again and the trend has been pretty firm. For the last several months we've stayed at a high level and continue to do so in early October," he added.
The housing sector has remained stubbornly strong this year despite a runup in interest rates which would normally be expected to limit sales and construction of new homes.
Although economists believe housing may be close to topping out, they said there is little evidence to suggest it will head decisively lower in the fourth quarter of the year.
"I see starts coming back in the months ahead," said Merrill Lynch's Dennis.
